title: Breaking: The Brood Is Back
description: Seventeen years on the dot, the cicadas come up out of the ground, and Snazzie FM covers it like a civil emergency. Ronnie keeps upgrading the decibel tier, the station's entomologist swears it's a textbook cycle right up until the bugs start coordinating, one caller keeps trying to feed them, and by the end the brood has appointed a spokesman.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We are cutting the regular hour on Snazzie FM. This is a breaking emergence. At four nineteen this afternoon, the ground opened up across the whole county, and folks, they are coming up. The brood is back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's cicadas, Ronnie. They do this. It's a calendar thing.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It is a calendar thing the way a tidal wave is a moon thing, Barry. <p:0.3> We are classifying this as a Tier One Acoustic Event. Let's go straight to our entomologist. Rhonda, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Thanks, Ronnie. So, great news, this is Brood Fourteen, right on schedule, seventeen years to the day. This is a textbook periodical emergence. Completely ordinary. Nothing here we haven't seen before.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Ordinary. <p:0.3> And what's the count, Rhonda?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: About a million per acre. Which is, again, totally normal for a brood.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A million per acre. <p:0.3> Folks, I'm upgrading us. We are now a Tier Two. Todd is on the roof with the meter. Todd, give me a number.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie. So I'm on the roof, and the meter says, um. <p:0.3> The meter says ninety four decibels, which is, that's a leaf blower. <p:0.4> But there's no leaf blower. It's just the air now. The air is ninety four.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's a normal bug summer, Todd. You get used to it by July.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hello, dear, yes, they're all over my porch, and oh, they're just precious. <p:0.3> I've put out a little dish for them. Cut up a banana. They've formed a line.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A line. <p:0.3> Mildred, do not feed the brood. Rhonda, do cicadas line up?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: No. <p:0.3> No, they, cicadas don't queue, they swarm, it's chaotic, that's the whole, hang on. <p:0.3> Mildred, when you say a line, do you mean a pile, or do you mean a line.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Single file, dear. Oldest in front. <p:0.3> They take turns at the banana.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Yeah, Ronnie, I'm driving through this, okay, and I gotta report the windshield is solid bug. <p:0.3> Wipers on. Wipers do nothing. <p:0.3> They are gripping the wipers. They want to stay on the wipers.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Just pull over and let them clear off, that's all you do with bugs.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Barry, I pulled over, and they all turned. <p:0.3> All of them. At once. To face the car. <p:0.3> Bugs don't have a front of the room, Barry, but they found one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: They found a front of the room. <p:0.3> Folks, that's an upgrade. We are now a Tier Three Coordinated Event. Bring the laundry in. Cover the banana, Mildred.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Why would she cover the banana, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Because the banana is how it started, Barry. A line forms at a banana. A line is the beginning of a society.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Okay, I need everyone calm, because the song is. <p:0.3> The song just changed. They sing in waves, it's mating, it's pulses, totally normal, except. <p:0.4> Pulses are random. This isn't random. This has a downbeat. They found the one.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: They've moved off the banana, dear. <p:0.3> They're at the window now. They've left the banana untouched and they're all just looking in. <p:0.3> They brought a second banana. I don't own a second banana.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Ronnie? <p:0.3> Update. The meter's reading one oh nine, but it's, it's pulsing in time now. Loud, quiet, loud, quiet. <p:0.4> And on the quiet part I can hear, I think they're saying a word.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A word. Rhonda, confirm. <p:0.3> Is the brood saying a word?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: I, the spectrogram, okay, the spectrogram's got a shape in it that shouldn't, that's a, that's a formant. <p:0.3> Bugs don't have formants, Ronnie. Vowels need a throat. <p:0.4> They've grown a vowel.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: They grew a vowel. The bugs grew a vowel.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: They moved my CAR, Barry! Not far, but I'm parked sideways now and the doors are shut and I did not do that! <p:0.3> They rocked it. <p:0.3> A million bugs leaned the same way at the same time like a stadium!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: They've taken a vote, dear! <p:0.3> They split into two groups on the lawn and one group got bigger and the other group flew off! That's a vote! I've seen a vote!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A vote. <p:0.3> Folks, bugs do not hold elections. I'm upgrading us one final time. As of this moment, the brood is, frankly, a constituency.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: The formant resolved, Ronnie. <p:0.3> I ran it through the software twice. The word is hello. <p:0.4> A million cicadas just learned the word hello and they're all saying it on the downbeat.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Okay so. <p:0.3> One of them came off the swarm. Down the antenna, onto the meter. It's bigger than the others. The others went quiet for it. <p:0.4> It's sitting on the meter like it owns the meter.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Bigger than the others. <p:0.3> Bigger how, Todd?

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Okay so it has the banana now. <p:0.3> The big one has Mildred's second banana and it set it down between us like, like a gift, and the swarm went dead silent. <p:0.4> I think this one's in charge.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: That's the front-of-the-line one!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: There's only one formant now!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Is the big one driving the swarm?!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It brought a banana to a meeting!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: It's clearing its throat!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's clearing its throat. <p:0.4> Folks. <p:0.3> We are no longer classifying this as an emergence. <p:0.3> We are classifying it as a guest.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I told you it was a calendar thing.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: It learned a second word, Ronnie. <p:0.3> The big one. After hello. <p:0.4> It said airtime. It's looking right at the meter and it said airtime.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then we put it on hold. <p:0.3> The brood has a spokesman, folks, and the spokesman wants the next segment. We'll be right back, soon as it finishes the banana.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Tell it there's more banana inside, dear.
